raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan.

I've been working these 6 mu for a long time now — since I was in my twenties, really. The land is what it is. My husband and I do most of the work ourselves, but for the wheat harvest and maize planting I usually pay the combine operator and the planter guy from the village. At my age, I can't be out there with a sickle anymore like when I was young.

**Wheat first, since that's what goes in the ground soonest after maize comes off.**

I plant winter wheat around October 10th, sometimes a few days later if the maize is slow to come off. I use Jimai variety seed — the agro-supply shop in town sells it, about 5-6 yuan per jin, and I put down maybe 18-20 jin per mu because my soil is a bit heavy and germination isn't always great. I don't save my own seed anymore; the extension guy years ago told us the saved seed loses vigor, and I believe him — I tried both and the bought seed does better.

For fertilizer, I buy the compound 15-15-15 for base fertilizer, about two bags for my 6 mu before planting, and then I topdress urea at jointing in March. My neighbor Old Wang does about the same. The extension folks say 15 kg N per mu is enough, but I usually end up around 17-18 because I'd rather waste a bit than see the wheat go yellow. Fertilizer's not cheap but a bad wheat crop is worse.

Irrigation — I water before winter (late November) to help overwintering, then at jointing, and usually one more time during grain filling if May is dry. The well is metered so I don't waste it, but you can't skip the jointing water, everyone knows that.

I expect maybe 420-450 kg/mu if the weather's normal. Last year I got 440.

**Then maize goes in right after wheat harvest, mid June, very tight turnaround.**

I use Zhengdan hybrid seed, what most people around here plant. The planter guy comes through and does it in an afternoon — no time to plant by hand, the wheat stubble is still warm. I don't till, just plant into the stubble. Saves time and the extension station says it's fine, keeps the moisture in.

Base fertilizer is compound with the seed, then I topdress urea at the big trumpet stage (around late July). Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat here — usually the summer rains handle most of it. I might irrigate once in August if it's dry during tasseling. Sometimes not at all.

For pests I watch for corn borer and armyworm. If I see them I spray, otherwise I don't bother. Herbicide yes, right after planting — can't weed 6 mu by hand anymore.

I expect 480-500 kg/mu for maize. It's a good crop for us.

**Total budget** — I don't have a notebook but in my head, inputs probably run 500-600 yuan per mu per year across both crops. On 6 mu that's about 3,300-3,500 yuan total. We have savings from selling the grain last year, it's manageable.
